screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: deep learning (nnU-Net), 3D volumetric processing, organ segmentation (lungs), CT modality, quantitative metrics (DSC, NSD), novel contribution (CTPA-specific model with external validation).

future_work: Develop and test the DL model in a large cohort of multiethnicity patients. Transfer learning to improve performance for both contrast and non-contrast imaging.

exclusion_reason: Only processes 2D slices without 3D context

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: deep learning primary, 3D CT volumes, organ segmentation, CT modality, quantitative metrics, novel contribution (ensemble segmentation+registration).

screening_notes: Deep learning primary method (InceptionResNetV2 + UNet3+), processes 3D CT volumes via multi-planar 2D networks combined into 3D, segments cardiac organs, uses CT, reports Dice and Hausdorff metrics, and presents a novel cascaded pipeline.
title: Automatic Cardiac Structure Contouring for Small Datasets with Cascaded Deep Learning Models
authors: L. B. van den Oever et al.

preprocessing: CT images converted to NUMPY, contrast adjusted to mediastinum window (W:350 HU, L:50 HU); no other preprocessing
postprocessing: Combination of three networks' outputs by multiplication of binary masks

limitations: Struggles with caudal and cranial parts of heart; difficulty near apex; underperforms for atria; non-contrast scans with thick slices and cardiac motion; ground truth variability.
future_work: Qualitative evaluations; training on contrast scans; possibly combining contrast and non-contrast scans.

screening_notes: Paper uses deep learning (2D and 3D U-Net) for segmentation of the prostatic urethra on planning CT images. It processes 3D volumes (3D U-Net) and reports quantitative metrics (centerline distance, PWR). Novel contribution: new method for prostatic urethra segmentation with large dataset. Meets all inclusion criteria.
title: Development of deep learning-based novel auto-segmentation for the prostatic urethra on planning CT images for prostate cancer radiotherapy
architecture_details: 2D U-Net: 3 residual units, channels 16,32,64,128,256; 3D U-Net: 4 residual units, channels 32,64,128,256,512. Implemented with MONAI.
loss_function: Dice Cross Entropy Loss (DiceCELoss)
preprocessing: Input data created from bladder and prostate contours (not CT images). DICOM RT Structure Set converted to binary images, resampled to 1mm voxel size, brightness values set (bladder=64, prostate=128). Output urethra=255. For 2D, projected 3D data in coronal and sagittal directions. Cropped to 128x128x128 (3D) or 256x256 (2D).
postprocessing: Predicted coordinates used to draw a circle of diameter 5mm on each CT slice, then resampled to original pixel size.
datasets: ["Tohoku University Hospital dataset (430 patients with localized prostate cancer)"]
dataset_size: 430 patients (70% training, 10% validation, 20% test)
comparison_methods: ["2D U-Net vs 3D U-Net", "Cubero et al. (deep learning on CT for brachytherapy)", "Belue et al. (deep learning on MRI)", "Takagi et al. (multi-atlas method)"]
training_time: Approximately 6 hours for 2D models, 24 hours for 3D model
limitations: Ground truth from urethral catheter may include deformation errors; cases with asymmetrical urethra due to prostate hypertrophy have reduced accuracy; some cases may have significant errors hindering clinical use.
future_work: Incorporate factors like benign prostatic hyperplasia; increase number of irregular cases; use MRI images to resolve catheter deformation.

screening_notes: The paper presents a hybrid method combining DL, atlas-based registration, and geometric models. DL is used only for the whole heart, not for the 17 other substructures. Although quantitative metrics are reported and CT is used, the primary segmentation method is not deep learning.
exclusion_reason: Deep learning is not the primary segmentation method. The proposed approach is a hybrid that uses deep learning (nnU-Net) only for whole heart segmentation, while the majority of cardiac substructures are segmented via multi-atlas mapping and geometric modeling. Thus, it does not meet the criterion of deep learning as the primary method.
title: Open-source, fully-automated hybrid cardiac substructure segmentation: development and optimisation

screening_notes: The proposed method uses a 2D SegNet architecture applied slice-by-slice to CT volumes, without 3D convolutions or volumetric context. It fails the 3D/volumetric processing criterion.
exclusion_reason: Only processes 2D slices without 3D context
title: Automatic Liver Segmentation from Multiphase CT Using Modified SegNet and ASPP Module
architecture_details: Modified SegNet with four encoder-decoder pairs, ASPP module (dilation rates 6, 12, 18), leaky ReLU activation, VGG-16 encoder initialization
loss_function: Cross entropy
preprocessing: Convert to Hounsfield units, convert to unsigned 8-bit, crop background, resize to 384x384x3, augmentation (scaling and translation)
postprocessing: None

future_work: Constructing a hepatic CADx system for differentiating between normal and abnormal liver and diagnosing liver cancer.

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: deep learning primary, 3D processing, organ segmentation, CT, quantitative metrics, novel contribution.
title: Deep learning-based whole-heart segmentation in 4D contrast-enhanced cardiac CT
architecture_details: Encoding path with two downsampling layers with strided convolutions, six residual ResNet blocks, decoding path with two upsampling layers with transposed convolutions, 3D batch normalization, softmax output.

screening_notes: The paper validates a commercial autocontouring model (RSL RayMachine) for head and neck OAR segmentation across different patient positions. It uses deep learning (3D CNN U-Net) and reports quantitative metrics (DSC, HD95, surface DSC), but it does not propose a new method or architecture. It is a clinical validation study, not a methodological contribution.
exclusion_reason: Only applies existing methods without methodological contribution; validation study of a commercial deep-learning model, no novel architecture or significant improvement presented.
title: Validation of a deep-learning segmentation model for adult and pediatric head and neck radiotherapy in different patient positions

screening_notes: The paper compares deep learning segmentation with deformable and rigid registration for autodelineation in proton therapy. While it uses CT scans and reports Dice/Hausdorff metrics, deep learning is only one of several methods evaluated, and the primary contribution is a workflow feasibility study rather than a novel deep learning method. Therefore, it does not meet criteria 1 and 6 for inclusion.
exclusion_reason: Deep learning is not the primary segmentation method; the paper evaluates multiple autodelineation methods (DLS, DIR, RIR) in a clinical workflow without proposing a novel deep learning architecture or significant methodological contribution.
title: Autodelineation methods in a simulated fully automated proton therapy workflow for esophageal cancer

screening_notes: Paper presents a modified 3D U-Net for kidney parenchyma segmentation in CT, reports Dice coefficient (0.89), uses 3D volumetric processing, and is a novel method. Meets all inclusion criteria.
title: Measurement of Glomerular Filtration Rate using Quantitative SPECT/CT and Deep-learning-based Kidney Segmentation
architecture_details: Modified 3D U-Net with pre-activation residual blocks, leaky ReLU, 3D spatial dropout (rate 0.3), element-wise sum array, symmetric skip connections
loss_function: Dice similarity coefficient
preprocessing: Resampled CT and SPECT images and manual VOIs to same matrix and voxel sizes (256x256x232, 1.726 mm^3), cropped to 192x128x96, applied 3D volume smoothing and morphological operations to manual VOIs
postprocessing: None mentioned

screening_notes: The paper demonstrates liver segmentation using a U-Net with VGG-11 backbone on the MSD Liver dataset, but the main novelty is the DP-SGD implementation. The segmentation task is used as a benchmark for the privacy framework, not as the primary contribution. Additionally, the input is 2D slices, not 3D volumes.
exclusion_reason: The paper's primary contribution is a differential privacy framework (deepee), not a novel 3D organ segmentation method. It processes 2D slices (256x256 images) from CT volumes rather than full 3D volumes, failing the 3D/volumetric criterion. The deep learning focus is on privacy-preserving training, not on segmentation architecture development.
title: Medical imaging deep learning with differential privacy

screening_notes: The paper presents a hybrid pipeline combining variational methods with a CNN for 3D segmentation of CT scans (aorta, abdominal organs) and MRI (brain tumors). Deep learning is a primary component, 3D volumes are processed, organs are segmented, CT is used, quantitative metrics are reported, and a novel hybrid method is proposed. Meets all inclusion criteria.
title: Evaluation of a hybrid pipeline for automated segmentation of solid lesions based on mathematical algorithms and deep learning
architecture_details: Hybrid pipeline combining a variational method (edge detection + intensity/location segmentation) with a CNN; CNN receives both the scan and the variational initial segmentation as input. Simplified networks with lighter architectures also tested in appendix.
loss_function: Not specified

postprocessing: Not specified

screening_notes: Paper presents a novel 3D U-Net variant (DA-UNet) with residual blocks, atrous inception, deep supervision, and CRF post-processing for liver segmentation from CT. screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: deep learning (CNN) is primary method, processes 3D CT volumes via multi-projection classification, segments kidney and spleen organs, uses CT modality, reports quantitative metrics (F1, VOE, RVD, ASSD, MSSD), and presents a novel method.
title: Localization of spleen and kidney organs from CT scans based on classification of slices in rotational views

preprocessing: Generation of learning data by extracting slices in X, Y, Z projections; scaling for RoiNetX and RoiNetY; point generation with spacing.
postprocessing: Adaptive fuzzy K-means clustering, morphological operations (dilation, hole filling, largest component selection).

dataset_size: 90 CT scans
comparison_methods: ["Graph-cut", "U-Net 3D", "nnUNet"]
inference_time: 3.25 s per 512x512 image; ROI generation 2.86 s per case
limitations: Higher implementation complexity; need for three networks; post-processing required; challenges with overlapping organ boundaries.

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: deep learning (3D U-Net + 2D U-Net) as primary method, processes 3D CT volumes, segments multiple heart structures (organs), reports Dice scores, and presents a novel framework combining deep learning with graph matching.
title: Graph matching and deep neural networks based whole heart and great vessel segmentation in congenital heart disease
architecture_details: Combines 3D U-Net for chambers and myocardium segmentation, 2D U-Net for blood pool segmentation, and graph matching for great vessel classification

preprocessing: ROI cropping, resizing to 64x64x64, data normalization, data augmentation (same as Ref.8)
postprocessing: Chambers and myocardium refinement using blood pool segmentation; graph matching for vessel classification; region growing for leftover vessels

comparison_methods: ["Seg-CNN (Payer et al.)"]
limitations: Limited GPU memory limits 3D U-net to down-sampled CT, boundary extraction errors in blood pool segmentation, threshold-based ground truth limits differentiation, lack of clinical-level criterion for training
future_work: Use more advanced GPUs to process larger dimensions, fusion/ensemble network, two-stage training strategy

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: deep learning (UNETR), 3D CT volumes, organ segmentation (liver), quantitative metrics (DSC, MSD, HD95), and novel contribution (fully automatic right lobe graft weight estimation).

screening_notes: Paper applies 3D nnU-Net to renal parenchyma and cortex segmentation for CKD evaluation. Meets criteria 1-5 (deep learning, 3D, organ segmentation, CT, quantitative metrics) but fails criterion 6 (novel contribution) and matches exclusion criterion 7.

screening_notes: The paper proposes a novel deep learning method (MetricUNet) for prostate segmentation from CT scans. future_work: Feed CNN with patches extracted from original CT volumes to avoid resampling and enlarge training set; collect more image data to improve performance and generalization; train a single DSD-UNET model to segment both anatomical structures and applicator simultaneously to streamline treatment planning workflow

screening_notes: Deep learning (SegNet) is the primary method for liver (organ) segmentation and the paper uses multiphase CT volumes with quantitative metrics (Dice 96.46% liver, 85.07% tumor), so criteria 1, 4, 5, 6 are met and the 'tumors only' exclusion does not apply (liver is segmented as an organ). However, the network is strictly 2D per-slice: the architecture table confirms 2D encoder/decoder feature maps (e.g., 380x380x64), slices are processed independently, and volumetric handling is limited to evaluating/summing per-slice results. This fails the mandatory 3D/volumetric inclusion criterion for a review on 3D organ segmentation.
exclusion_reason: Only processes 2D slices without 3D context (exclusion criterion 3): the SegNet architecture operates on individual 2D slices (380x380x3 input, 2D convolutions, per-slice preprocessing/resizing) with no 3D convolutions or inter-slice context; tumor segmentation via K-means is likewise intensity-based 2D per-slice processing.

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: (1) DL primary method (FCN with VGG16 backbone, pixel-to-label training); (2) processes 3D CT volumes — 2D sections sampled in three orthogonal planes, then fused via voxel-wise 3D majority voting (3D-2D-3D transformation), so not 2D-only; (3) segments 19 anatomical structures (liver, kidneys, spleen, pancreas, lungs, etc.); (4) CT modality; (5) quantitative evaluation (88.1%/87.9% voxel labeling accuracy on train/test — voxel accuracy rather than Dice); (6) novel contribution (cross-sectional FCN voting scheme, FCN2s variant with skip-based deconvolution). Not a survey, not tumor-only, clearly methodological. Note: text is truncated mid-experiments; per-organ Dice, training/inference times, limitations sections not visible in provided content.
title: Deep learning of the sectional appearances of 3D CT images for anatomical structure segmentation based on an FCN voting method
architecture: FCN (fully convolutional network) with VGG16 backbone
architecture_details: VGG16 down-sampling path with FC layers converted to convolutions; up-sampling path with deconvolution layers and skip connections (FCN32s, FCN16s, FCN8s, FCN4s, FCN2s variants trained sequentially); 3D-2D-3D transformation: 2D sections sampled in axial/sagittal/coronal directions, segmented by the single 2D FCN, stacked back to 3D and fused by voxel-wise majority voting; transfer learning from ImageNet-pretrained VGG16; ReLU activation, dropout (0.5), local contrast normalization in deconv layers; no 3D convolutions used
loss_function: Sum of pixel-wise losses between network prediction and human-annotated label map (pixel-to-label training; exact loss type not specified in provided text)
preprocessing: 12-bit one-channel CT gray levels linearly interpolated to 8-bit (0-255) and duplicated across RGB channels for VGG16 input; no other normalization applied
postprocessing: Voxel-wise majority voting over the three orthogonal 2D labelings; ties broken by selecting the organ with largest volume (anatomical prior)
dataset_size: 240 CT scans with ground truth (from 200 patients; 89 torso, 17 chest, 134 abdomen/pelvis); 95% training / 5% testing (12 test scans); ~100,000 derived 2D sections for training

screening_notes: The paper otherwise satisfies most criteria: deep learning (DDCNN, a modified VGG-16 with dilated convolution modules) is the primary method; planning CT scans are used; it segments the CTV plus OARs (bladder, left/right femoral heads, intestine, colon); it reports quantitative DSC metrics (e.g., CTV 87.7%, bladder 93.4%); and it presents a novel architecture with clear contributions (front-end/back-end dilated convolution, CLAHE preprocessing, first CNN-based CTV segmentation for rectal cancer radiotherapy). However, the authors explicitly state the network is 2D and operates slice-by-slice independently, with no 3D context aggregation or volumetric processing, matching the exclusion criterion 'Only processes 2D slices without 3D context' and failing the inclusion requirement to 'process 3D CT volumes (not just 2D slices independently)'.
exclusion_reason: Only processes 2D slices without 3D context (Exclusion criterion 3; fails Inclusion criterion 2). The paper explicitly describes 'a novel 2D DDCNN model' that segments ROIs 'in 2D CT images slice by slice' using 2D convolutions (3x3 filters, 353x353 slice input) with no 3D/volumetric convolutions or inter-slice context modeling.

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: (1) DL-CNN is the primary method, driving the segmentation via a likelihood map used in cascaded level sets; (2) volumetric processing — CNN is applied slice-wise but likelihood maps are stacked into a 3D map and segmented with 3D cascaded level sets against 3D hand-segmented reference volumes; (3) segments the bladder (organ wall), not tumors — lesion analysis is only for containment checking; (4) CT urography; (5) quantitative metrics (volume intersection, volume error, average distance); (6) novel contribution — new inner+outer wall method significantly outperforming prior CLASS and ITK-SNAP. Caveat: no 3D convolutions (is_3d=false per schema definition) and no Dice reported (volume intersection ratio used as overlap metric), which lowers confidence slightly.
title: Deep-Learning Convolutional Neural Network: Inner and Outer Bladder Wall Segmentation in CT Urography
architecture_details: 5-layer CNN: 2 convolutional layers (64 kernels 5x5), 2 locally-connected convolutional layers (64 and 32 kernels 3x3), 1 fully-connected layer, Softmax 2-class output; ReLU, overlapping pooling, local response normalization (N=9, tau=0.001, eps=0.75). 16x16 pixel ROIs with central 8x8 'jittering' labeling. CNN likelihood map used as speed term F(phi) in the 4th of four cascaded 3D level sets, followed by 2D level set refinement per slice.

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: (1) U-Net-based deep learning is the primary method; (2) includes a true 3D U-DL variant with 3x3x3 convolutions processing 192-slice CT volumes, plus 2D U-DL stacked into 3D likelihood maps (note: best-performing model was the 2D U-DL); (3) segments the bladder (organ); (4) CT urography (CT) modality; (5) quantitative metrics reported (AVI, AVE, AAVE, AMD, AHD, AJI); (6) novel contribution — modified U-Net architecture (padded convs, changed concatenation position), systematic 2D-vs-3D/resolution/cropping ablations, and statistically significant improvement (p<0.001) over DCNN-LS baseline and two non-DL methods. title: U-Net-based Deep-Learning Bladder Segmentation in CT Urography

loss_function: Binary cross-entropy (Adam optimizer, lr=0.0001)
preprocessing: Automated center cropping (256x256 from 512x512 slices, or 128x128 from 256x256 downsampled); optional downsampling via 2x2 box filter stride 2; radiologist-marked first/last bladder slice to limit volume extent (192-slice stack centered in z for 3D U-DL)
postprocessing: Likelihood map thresholded at 0.2; largest connected component retained as bladder region and converted to binary mask

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: (1) primary method is a deep CNN (3D U-Net variants); (2) fully volumetric 3D convolutions on CT volumes with a localization-crop-segment workflow; (3) segments 5 thoracic OARs (lungs, heart, esophagus, spinal cord); (4) CT modality (AAPM 2017 challenge + private UK dataset); (5) quantitative evaluation with Dice, MSD, and 95% Hausdorff distance; (6) novel contribution via cascaded localization+individual organ networks on cropped patches and a novel multi-crop testing augmentation (1st place in AAPM challenge ongoing phase). title: Deep convolutional neural network for segmentation of thoracic organs-at-risk using cropped 3D images
architecture: 3D U-Net (cascaded: multi-label localization network + individual binary organ segmentation networks)
architecture_details: Three-step workflow: (a) multi-label 3D U-Net (6-class) on downsampled/center-cropped images for organ localization; (b) separate binary 3D U-Nets per organ trained on cropped patches containing one organ each, with randomized bounding-box margins (alpha/beta 0.1-0.7) as training augmentation; (c) testing augmentation averaging 6 differently cropped inputs per organ. 3 encoding/decoding blocks, two sets of 3x3x3 convs with batch normalization and ReLU per block; attempts with residual U-Net and dilated convolutions did not improve performance
loss_function: Weighted cross-entropy (localization: background 1.0, spinal cord 2.0, right lung 1.0, left lung 1.0, heart 1.0, esophagus 2.0; spinal cord network 2.0 foreground/1.0 background; esophagus network 3.0/1.0). Dice loss and combined CE+Dice loss experimented but weighted CE retained due to instability of Dice loss in localization network
preprocessing: Uniform resampling to 0.9756x0.9756x3 mm voxel spacing; in-plane matrix fixed to 512x512 (zero-padded or center-cropped); HU clipping to [-1000, 600]; intensity normalization to [0, 1]; label maps generated through the same pipeline
postprocessing: Keep largest connected 3D component per organ (remove isolated false-positive regions); conflict resolution for overlapping organs by maximum probability >0.5; resampling to original dimensions; contour extraction via marching squares into DICOM-RT format
datasets: ["2017 AAPM Thoracic Auto-segmentation Challenge", "University of Kentucky (UK) private dataset"]

training_time: 8 hours (localization network); 7-11 hours per organ segmentation network; 200 epochs each

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: (1) deep learning (FCN-8s) is the primary segmentation engine, integrated with active contour models; (2) task and evaluation are volumetric/3D liver segmentation from CT volumes with 3D surface-distance metrics, although the FCN backbone operates on 2D axial slices (2D convolutions only; 3D extension explicitly described as future work) — borderline on the '3D context' criterion but included because the pipeline targets whole-volume liver segmentation and is evaluated volumetrically; (3) segments liver (parenchyma; tumor masks merged into liver reference for LiTS); (4) CT modality; (5) quantitative metrics reported (Dice, ASSD/RMSD/MaxSD, meanIU, pixel accuracy); (6) novel contribution: adaptive FCN-derived external steering force for active contour models enabling distant initialization and topology preservation. title: Automatic Liver Segmentation by Integrating Fully Convolutional Networks into Active Contour Models
authors: Xiaotao Guo et al. (Guo, Schwartz, Zhao)
architecture: FCN-8s integrated into active contour models (ACM)
architecture_details: Modified FCN-8s (Long et al.) with output channels changed from 21 to 7 to predict a layered label map for the liver (interior/exterior narrow-band layers around boundary + interior/exterior regional layers) derived from signed distance transforms; the structured FCN output is converted into an adaptive external steering force (strength increases with distance to boundary via polynomial/exponential function; direction depends on inside/outside) added to a localizing region-based active contour (Lankton et al.) with curvature smoothing, evolved via sparse-field level set (Whitaker); allows initialization far from the liver boundary and topology control
loss_function: Per-pixel unnormalized softmax loss (same as original FCN-8s)
preprocessing: Axial slices at 512x512; DICOM pixel spacing extracted to adaptively define narrow-band widths in mm; binary segmentation masks converted to 7-category layered label maps via Euclidean distance transform (signed distance / level set representation)
postprocessing: FCN output thresholded to obtain initial binary contour; active contour (level set, sparse-field) refinement enforces boundary smoothness, excludes spurious fragments, and allows topology-preserving evolution
datasets: ["Columbia University Medical Center clinical liver CT dataset (in-house)", "SLIVER07 training set", "LiTS (MICCAI 2017 Liver Tumor Segmentation Challenge) training set"]
dataset_size: In-house: 77 CT scans per Methods (abstract states 73), split 42 train / 19 eval / 16 test; SLIVER07: 20 scans; LiTS: 131 scans (external validation)

other_metrics: {"FCN-alone pixel accuracy (train/test)": "99.07% / 99.00%", "FCN-alone mean accuracy (train/test)": "74.87% / 71.70%", "FCN-alone mean IU (train/test)": "63.78% / 60.75%", "surface distances": "Average symmetric surface distance (ASSD), root mean square symmetric surface distance (RMSD), and maximum symmetric surface distance (MaxSD) in mm reported per dataset (Table 1)", "mean relative DICE improvement over FCN alone": "1.8% (SLIVER07), 1.5% (LiTS)"}
comparison_methods: ["FCN alone (thresholded FCN-8s output)", "Global region-based active contour (Chan-Vese)", "Localizing region-based active contour (Lankton & Tannenbaum)"]
limitations: Current convolutional networks still have difficulty with irregularly shaped livers, missing small objects, severe disease near the liver boundary, and adjacent structures with liver-like intensity (Fig. 11); performance depends on tuning of force weights (curvature, external force, image force) and local region radius; in-house training dataset relatively small; FCN operates on 2D slices (3D extension proposed but not implemented); label inconsistencies in FCN output (spurious spots) not yet exploited for cleanup
future_work: Enlarge the liver dataset with more challenging cases; develop an attention mechanism to focus the network on errors; exploit multi-layer label inconsistency to clean spurious spots; extend to true 3D processing (3D FCN training, narrow bands as surfaces) and multi-organ segmentation (e.g., liver and spleen simultaneously)

screening_notes: Passes criteria 1, 4, 5, 6: deep learning is the primary method (cascaded ResNet18 CNNs combined via Boosting), CT modality, segments anatomical organs-at-risk (parotids, thyroids, optic nerves — not tumors), reports DSC/95%HD/VOE, and presents a novel cascaded Boosting framework. Fails the 3D requirement: segmentation is strictly 2D patch-based — 'patch-level learning by sliding windows in the 2D space of images', with 2D patches (31x31 to 71x71) classifying the center pixel per axial slice. No 3D convolutions, no inter-slice/ volumetric context anywhere in the method. Volumetric DSC is computed only as post-hoc evaluation over stacked slices, which does not constitute 3D processing. Study type not assigned since paper is excluded.

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: (1) Primary method is deep learning - four 3D fully convolutional U-Net variants (LC-net, MC-net, MI-net, late fusion) with optional residual blocks; (2) 3D volumetric processing via 32x32x32 patches and 3D convolutions; (3) Segments six anatomical organs (lungs, liver, spleen, kidneys); (4) DECT (dual-energy CT) is a CT modality, acquired with Siemens SOMATOM Definition Force; (5) Reports Dice, Hausdorff distance, and AUC with fivefold cross-validation; (6) Novel contribution: systematic comparison of dual-energy information fusion strategies in network architectures plus residual blocks and a weighted Dice loss with boundary compensation. No exclusion criteria apply.
title: Automatic multi-organ segmentation in dual-energy CT (DECT) with dedicated 3D fully convolutional DECT networks
architecture: 3D fully convolutional network (3D U-Net-based) with four dual-energy fusion variants: LC-net (linear combination), MC-net (multi-channel), MI-net (multi-image/two-branch), and late fusion
architecture_details: Best performing variant was MI-net (two FCN branches extracting per-energy features fused at bottom level); residual blocks based on identity mapping with dimension matching (He et al.) and full pre-activation; skip connection concatenating original-level features; trainable fusion weights; softmax output with argmax
loss_function: Weighted multi-class Dice loss with median frequency balancing and boundary compensation terms (balance weight k)

postprocessing: Per-voxel argmax over class probabilities; largest connected component filtering to remove wrongly classified voxels

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: (1) deep learning primary method (cascaded V-Net + novel 2.5D SINet); (2) volumetric processing with explicit 3D context — 3D V-Nets for localization, 3×3×3 kernels, slice correlation module for cross-slice non-local interaction, tri-view ensemble + recurrent refinement (not 2D-slices-only); (3) organ segmentation (pancreas); (4) CT (NIH Pancreas-CT, 82 contrast-enhanced 3D CT scans); (5) quantitative metrics (Dice 86.21±4.37%, sensitivity, specificity, 4-fold CV); (6) multiple novel contributions (Square Root Dice loss, Slice Shuffle self-supervised pre-training, Slice Correlation Module). Not a review, not tumor-only, not framework/tooling paper.
title: Improving the Slice Interaction of 2.5D CNN for Automatic Pancreas Segmentation
architecture: Two-stage coarse-to-fine: cascaded 3D V-Nets (localization) + 2.5D Slice Interaction Network (SINet) with Slice Correlation Module (refinement)
architecture_details: Localization: two cascaded V-Nets on downsampled volume then cropped 3D bounding box. Refinement: three SINets along axial/coronal/sagittal views (encoder with asymmetric 3×3×1 and symmetric 3×3×3 convs, instance norm, 4 deep-supervision decode paths), Slice Correlation Module using bilinear pooling (second-order attention) for non-local cross-slice interaction, PNet fusion net, recurrent refinement (stop at 95% Dice similarity or 5 iterations). Slice Shuffle self-supervised pre-training on 5 stacked slices with margin 3.
loss_function: Dice loss; Square Root Dice (SRDice) loss (localization recall boost); L1 reconstruction loss (slice shuffle pretext task); summed deep-supervision loss over decode paths
preprocessing: Pixel values clipped to [-100, 240] and rescaled to [0, 255]; central crop to 360×320×L; down-sampling by factor 2 for localization; data augmentation: random crop/pad [0.8-1.2] (loc) and [0.6-1.4] (ref), random rotation ±15°, elastic transformation, slice perturbation
postprocessing: Threshold binarization at 0.5; 3D bounding box crop with 16-voxel margin; 2D bounding box extension factor 1.2; connected domain analysis (largest connected region)
dataset_size: 82 abdominal contrast-enhanced 3D CT scans (53 male, 27 female; avg age 46.8±16.7)
dice_per_organ: {"pancreas": "86.21±4.37% (fully automatic, 4-fold CV); 88.14% with oracle 2D bounding boxes; ablation: SINet w/o slice interaction 84.87%, from scratch 85.69%"}
comparison_methods: ["Zeng et al. (HDC)", "Zhao et al. (two-stage 3D CNN)", "Chen et al. (2D+3D)", "Man et al. (deep Q-learning + geometry-aware U-Net)", "Yu et al. (ReSE-Net)", "Zhu et al. (3D coarse-to-fine)", "Cai et al. (PNet/RNN)", "Xia et al. (Volumetric Fusion Net)", "Zhou et al. (fixed-point model)", "Liu et al.", "Yang et al.", "Fang et al. (progressive fusion)"]
inference_time: Not reported (authors note coarse-to-fine is slower than one-stage)
limitations: Most misclassified voxels stem from localization errors — high sensitivity but low specificity, with duodenum frequently misclassified as pancreas in the head region; texture variations from vessels, pancreatic duct, and steatosis cause failures (e.g., missed pancreatic tail); coarse-to-fine pipeline takes more time than one-stage segmentation, limiting real-time use.
future_work: Replace second V-Net with deep Q-learning-based detection; investigate generative models for data augmentation to handle special textures; combine slice shuffle with other pretext tasks (e.g., denoising); develop more efficient weight-allocation strategies for ensemble fusion.

title: Complete Abdomen and Pelvis Segmentation using U-Net Variant Architecture

postprocessing: None reported

screening_notes: Fails S3#3 despite meeting all other criteria (CNN primary method, CT modality, multi-organ, quantitative metrics, novel architecture). The paper is explicit in its own limitations section: 'it did not utilize the information between adjacent slices... such information can be exploited if we use 3D models. We will extend and improve our ARPM-net to perform 3D volume segmentation in our future work.' The network is a 2D multi-residual U-net applied slice-by-slice (loss defined over H×W, timing reported per-image). The '3D max-pooling' inside the MRF block is a local kernel operation, not inter-slice context. This paper belongs in the 2D-only exclusion pile, not the 3D review corpus.
exclusion_reason: Only processes 2D slices without 3D context (exclusion criterion 3).

screening_notes: All other criteria are satisfied: deep learning is the primary method (SW-DNN, a novel stochastic-width modification of DeepLabv3+); CT modality is used (150 planning CT scans from West China Hospital); quantitative metrics are reported (DSC 0.7457 2D / 0.7530 3D, TPVF, PPV, with t-tests); and there is a clear methodological contribution (SW mechanism on shortcut connections). However, the two disqualifying criteria are unambiguous: the network is strictly 2D slice-based despite volumetric metric evaluation, and CTV delineation is target-volume (tumor-inclusive) segmentation rather than organ segmentation, which is out of scope for a review on 3D organ segmentation. No extraction performed per protocol.
exclusion_reason: Fails inclusion criteria 2 (3D/volumetric) and 3 (organ segmentation). (1) The SW-DNN (DeepLabv3+/ResNet101 variant) processes 2D CT slices independently: the input is explicitly defined as x ∈ R^(w×h), data augmentation is applied per-slice ('the CT slice was randomly flipped horizontally'), and there are no 3D convolutions or volumetric context. Although the authors report '3D-based evaluations' of DSC/TPVF/PPV, this only means volumetric metrics were computed after stacking 2D slice predictions — the model itself has no 3D context (exclusion criterion 3). (2) The segmentation target is the clinical target volume (CTV) for stomach cancer radiotherapy, described as 'tissues of potential tumors or subclinical diseases that are barely detectable in CT images' — a radiotherapy target/tumor-related volume, not an anatomical organ (exclusion criterion 5).

title: Automatic delineation of cardiac substructures using a region-based fully convolutional network

postprocessing: Mask-score weighted consolidation/averaging of overlapping ROI predictions per voxel; 3x3 boxcar filter used for visualization only; heart-constrained contour removal suggested as future clinical postprocessing (not applied)

screening_notes: The paper meets most criteria: deep learning is the primary method (SANet with HRNet-w18 encoder, novel Scale Attention Module), organs (colon, small intestine, duodenum) are segmented from CT with quantitative metrics (DSC, HD95, RVD, CD). However, the model is strictly 2D: 'All the 3D CT scans were converted into 2D slices for model training' and 'all CT scans were inferred in a slice-by-slice manner. Then the slices from the same scan were stacked into a 3D volume for evaluation.' No 3D convolutions or interslice context are used; stacking is performed only post-hoc for volumetric metric computation. The authors themselves list as a limitation that 'the proposed 2D input for SANet might cause some loss of spatial information and consistency along z-direction compared with 3D input.' This is 2D-slice-independent processing, explicitly excluded by criterion 3. Slight residual ambiguity because evaluation is volumetric and 3D visualizations are provided, hence confidence 0.85 rather than higher.
exclusion_reason: Only processes 2D slices without 3D context (Exclusion Criterion 3; fails Inclusion Criterion 2)

screening_notes: Paper meets several criteria: deep learning (U-Net CNN) is the primary method, CT modality (contrast-enhanced renal CT), kidney segmentation (organ-level, plus tumor/cyst), and extensive quantitative evaluation (Dice, ASD, RCC, RIU, UA). However, it fails the 3D/volumetric requirement: the model is an explicitly acknowledged 2D architecture with no 3D convolution or volumetric context. Additionally, the contribution is primarily a comparative evaluation of existing uncertainty quantification techniques (MC Dropout, DropConnect, ensembles, TTA) on a standard benchmark U-Net rather than a novel segmentation architecture (weakening Inclusion criterion 6 / triggering Exclusion criterion 7), though this is secondary to the decisive 2D-processing exclusion. Not a framework paper (no open-source toolkit presented), so framework routing/template not applicable.
exclusion_reason: Only processes 2D slices without 3D context (Exclusion criterion 3). The paper explicitly uses a 2D VGG16 U-Net applied to independently processed 2D slices (resampled to 128×128 pixels; 16,151 2D training images), and the authors state: 'The main limitation of this study lies in the implementation of a 2D architecture, when several 3D networks have been already effectively proposed for this purpose.' While Dice is computed over whole 3D volumes for evaluation, the network architecture and inference operate purely per-slice with no 3D context, failing Inclusion criterion 2.

screening_notes: Meets all 6 inclusion criteria: (1) deep learning primary (DQN-based RL agents + 3D U-Net/Attention U-Net/Swin U-Netr); (2) 3D volumetric processing (64×64×64 patches, 3D architectures); (3) pancreas organ subregions (head/neck/body/tail) + pancreatic duct — organ structures, not tumors/lesions; (4) CT modality (two CT datasets); (5) quantitative DSC with per-organ breakdown and statistical tests; (6) novel contribution — first CT segmentation of all four pancreatic subregions without presegmented pancreas, novel combination of RL landmark detection + landmark-guided registration + probability-map-augmented U-Net. title: Reinforcement learning-based anatomical maps for pancreas subregion and duct segmentation
architecture: Multiagent RL (DQN) landmark detection + landmark-guided nonrigid registration + U-Net segmentation (3D U-Net, Attention U-Net, Swin U-Netr)
architecture_details: Single-agent DQN detects whole-pancreas center; collaborative multiagent DQN (adapted from Vlontzos et al., shared conv layers, independent FC layers, communication via Qm/Qe functions) detects subregion centers and duct start/center/end landmarks; detected landmarks drive nonrigid registration of annotated atlases to generate probability maps Ps (4-channel subregions) and Pd (1-channel duct); probability maps concatenated with CT input to U-Net variants; final mask S = P^λ · R thresholded
loss_function: DQN Bellman/Q-learning loss (Eq. 3) for RL agents; segmentation training loss not explicitly specified
preprocessing: Data augmentation: flip and rotation (10% random probability), random intensity shift (50% probability); patch-based training with 64×64×64 patches; Adam optimizer (lr 1e-4, weight decay 1e-5), cyclical learning rate schedule, 30,000 iterations
postprocessing: Element-wise weighting of raw segmentation with probability maps (S = P^λ · R, λ tuned on validation set), then thresholding to binary masks (threshold also tuned on validation)
datasets: ["NIH Pancreas-CT (TCIA, Roth et al.)", "Private pancreatic duct dataset (Innopolis University ethical approval)"]
dataset_size: 82 CT scans (pancreatic subregions) + 37 CT scans (pancreatic duct); splits 62:10:10 and 22:5:10

comparison_methods: ["3D U-Net (baseline, CT only)", "Attention U-Net (baseline, CT only)", "Swin U-Netr (baseline, CT only)", "Intensity-based atlas registration", "Cascaded SE-Dense U-Net (Shen et al.)", "PA guided network (Shen et al.)", "Multiscale PA guided network (Shen et al.)", "Multiphase Alignment Ensemble (Xia et al.)", "Hyper-pairing network / 3D-ResDSN variants (Zhou et al.)"]

postprocessing: None — single forward pass, no atlases, priors, or post-hoc heuristics

title: PC-U Net: Learning to Jointly Reconstruct and Segment the Cardiac Walls in 3D from CT Data
architecture: PC-U Net: U-Net-style image encoder + PointNet branch + mask decoder
architecture_details: Three-part network: (1) image encoder with 3D convolutions (PointOutNet-style) reconstructing a 4096-point 3D point cloud; (2) PointNet (MLP 32/128/512 channels + global max-pooling + FC layers) extracting point features; (3) mask decoder reconstructing dense segmentation from point features, with encoder skip connections combined via voxel-wise multiplication. Variants tested with 2D and 3D convolutions; 3D conv is the best model.
loss_function: Chamfer loss (point cloud reconstruction) + soft Dice loss (segmentation), combined as Loss = lp + λ·ls with λ=0.001 (grid-searched)
preprocessing: LV ROI cropping; resampling to 1.0 mm isotropic; resize to fixed (128,128,64); intensity divided by 2048 and clamped to [-1,1]; elastic deformation augmentation ×200 (20 → 4,000 samples); ground-truth point clouds generated from mesh vertices, centered at origin, downsampled to N=4096

screening_notes: The paper meets criteria 1 (DL is primary method: U-Net backbone with Res-SE blocks), 3 (segments 11 thoracic OARs: lungs, trachea, bronchial tree, aorta, heart, esophagus, liver, humeral heads, spinal cord), 4 (planning CT scans from 500 patients), and 5 (quantitative metrics: vDSC 0.896 for AI, HD95 5.62 mm, sDSC, contouring time). However, it fails criterion 2: the Discussion explicitly states 'the model's 2D architecture', and no 3D convolutions or 3D contextual processing are described; evaluation is volumetric but the method itself is 2D slice-based. Furthermore, the architectural description is minimal (details deferred to supplementary tables), the code is proprietary and not available, and the core novelty is trial design/clinical evidence (physician-AI interaction, variability reduction, dosimetric impact) rather than a methodological contribution to 3D organ segmentation. Borderline aspects noted: it benchmarks against 3D methods (nnU-Net vDSC 0.850, TotalSegmentator vDSC 0.781), which a lenient reading could justify inclusion; hence confidence is 0.8 rather than higher.
exclusion_reason: Fails criterion 2 (3D/Volumetric): the iCurveE model is explicitly described by the authors as having a '2D architecture' (U-Net backbone with Res-SE blocks), i.e., 2D slice-based processing with no 3D context reported — matching exclusion criterion 3 ('Only processes 2D slices without 3D context'). Additionally, the paper's contribution is prospective clinical validation of a pre-existing, proprietary commercial auto-segmentation tool (iCurveE, NMPA Class III approved, developed by PVmed on a separate retrospective dataset), not a novel segmentation method or architecture (include criterion 6 not met; exclude criterion 7 arguably applies).

title: A pipeline for automated deep learning liver segmentation (PADLLS) from contrast enhanced CT exams
architecture: PADLLS: cascade of Dense V-net (Gibson et al.) and H-DenseUnet (Li et al.) with knowledge-based heuristics
architecture_details: Stage 1: Dense V-net (144x144x144 input, dense feature stacks, spatial prior, 9 classes) segments liver/stomach/spleen; stomach+spleen voxels set to -100 HU; V-net liver mask defines H-DenseUnet bounding box. Ascites correction: 15 HU threshold (ROC-optimized) + morphological opening (disk r=2) + 1500-pixel area filter. Stage 2: H-DenseUnet (224x224x12 input; 2D DenseUnet on 3-slice stacks + 3D DenseUnet + Hybrid Fusion layer, ~80M params) yields final segmentation.
loss_function: V-net: probabilistic Dice score function as L2 regularization loss with explicit spatial prior; H-DenseUnet: weighted cross-entropy
preprocessing: Rotation 90 deg clockwise + reflection about vertical axis; DICOM/MHD to NIfTI conversion; SLIVER07 RAW/MHD first converted to DICOM; bounding box crop from V-net output resized to 224x224x12
postprocessing: Truncate to slices containing liver pixels; exclude <0 HU pixels (lung removal); largest-object volume filtering; image closing with disk r=2 and sphere r=3; hole filling; liver+tumor masks combined into single liver volume
datasets: ["SLIVER07", "3DIRCADb", "Cancer Imaging Archive Pancreas-CT (V-net training)", "BTCV Segmentation Challenge (V-net training)", "LiTS (component training)", "3 multiphase CT scans (ascites test)"]
dataset_size: ~220+ abdominal CT scans across component training (>90 for V-net, >130 for H-DenseUnet); evaluated on 20 SLIVER07 + 20 3DIRCADb + 3 multiphase scans

title: Deformable multi-head cross attention-based 3D U-net for context-aware multi-modal cardiac image segmentation with uncertainty-aware maps

title: Submanifold Sparse Convolutional Networks for Automated 3D Segmentation of Kidneys and Kidney Tumours in Computed Tomography
architecture: 3D Submanifold Sparse Convolutional U-Net (SSCN), two-stage pipeline
architecture_details: Stage 1: low-resolution sparse U-Net for ROI detection; Stage 2: high-resolution sparse U-Net for refined segmentation. Fully convolutional encoder-decoder with ConvNeXtV2 blocks; six encoder stages (features 16-512, depths 2,4,4,8,8,8); skip connections via element-wise summation; deep supervision on last three decoder stages; sigmoid multi-label output (3 channels: kidneys+masses, tumour+cyst, tumour); 27,473,696 parameters; built on MinkowskiEngine v0.5.4 with a custom fork adding CUDA depth-wise convolution kernels; AdamW optimizer (lr 5e-4, weight decay 1e-5), 500 epochs/fold, batch size 1 with gradient accumulation over 8, cosine annealing; hyperparameters tuned with Optuna
loss_function: Dice loss with weighted deep supervision (weight 1/2^i per decoder level)
preprocessing: Resampling to isotropic voxel sizes: 1.99 mm (Stage 1) and 0.78 mm (Stage 2); voxel sparsification via HU thresholds derived from 0.5th/99.5th percentiles of segmentation voxels (-53.4 to 283.2 HU), retaining ~99% of segmentation voxels and removing 76.8% of background; ROI-based cropping of high-resolution scans; MONAI data augmentation pipeline (affine transforms, flipping, intensity scaling/shifting, Gaussian noise/smoothing)
postprocessing: Probability thresholding (>0.1) for ROI definition; elliptical dilation (11 voxels) of Stage-1 ROI; removal of small disconnected regions (<50 voxels); connected component analysis to split scans into K independently processed components; no post-processing applied to final segmentation masks (explicitly noted)
dataset_size: 489 CT scans (training subset used; full challenge set 599 with 110 held-out test; 5-fold cross-validation)

title: DRAN: Deep recurrent adversarial network for automated pancreas segmentation
architecture: DRAN: deep recurrent adversarial network (segmentation network as generator + discriminative network)
architecture_details: Three modules: (1) dilated convolution autoencoder (DCAE) with new adaptive dilated blocks (ADB) at dilation rates 4 and 8, separable 1x3/3x1 convolutions (~30% memory saving); (2) Local-LSTM module operating on patch-wise sequences serialised via a Hilbert space-filling curve; (3) adversarial module (discriminator with 5x5 convs) for inter-slice smoothness; 103M parameters vs 296M (U-Net) and 158M (FCN)
loss_function: Laplacian-smoothed DSC loss (segmentation) + hybrid discriminative loss (binary cross-entropy + perceptual loss); joint adversarial minimax optimisation
preprocessing: Area-sensitive candidate region generation via modified RPN (label expansion for ~1:3 positive:negative ratio, ~100% recall); resize to 224x160; per-CT normalisation (x - mean)/var; no denoising; no data augmentation
postprocessing: None reported

title: Interactive 3D U-net for the segmentation of the pancreas in computed tomography scans
authors: T G W Boers et al.
architecture_details: U-Net extended with 3D convolutional filters, padding (1,1,1) to preserve feature map size. Fully trained baseline for initial segmentation; in interactive mode, last layer plus a layer in the deepest encoder-decoder (latent) section are retrained on user scribbles (transfer learning), remaining layers frozen. Compared against iFCN (Wang et al. 2018 dilated FCN) and the Çiçek et al. 2016 3D U-Net.
loss_function: Differentiable soft Dice loss (Milletari et al. 2016), averaged over classes; interactive loss = voxel-weight-map-weighted Dice (scribble voxels weight 3, voxels within geodesic-distance threshold 0.2 of scribbles weight 0) plus a volume-difference penalty term (lambda-weighted)
preprocessing: Gaussian smoothing filter (sigma 0.75); HU window rescaling from [-160, 240] HU to [-1, 1] with clipping; automatic bounding-box crop around reference segmentation with 5% margin; trilinear resampling to 64x64x24 voxels. Data augmentation: ~1000-fold with random translations (+/-3 voxels), rotations (+/-10 degrees), Gaussian noise (sigma 0-3 HU).
postprocessing: None described for iUnet (authors explicitly avoid the organ-specific post-processing used by iFCN, which was inadequate for pancreas)

screening_notes: Novel deep learning method (PBR-UNet) for pancreas segmentation from CT volumes. Passes all inclusion criteria: (1) DL is primary method (FCN initial estimation + 2.5D UNet with bi-directional recurrent optimization); (2) not purely slice-independent — core contribution is inter-slice context via probabilistic-map-guided multi-channel data and bi-directional recurrent forward/backward propagation across slices (2.5D local 3D hybrid information); (3) segments pancreas organ; (4) CT only (NIH Pancreas-CT, MSD pancreas); (5) quantitative metrics reported (DSC 85.35% NIH 4-CV, 85.65% MSD, ASD, HD95, precision/recall/IOU); (6) novel architecture contribution. No exclusion criteria triggered. Note: no 3D convolutions used (2.5D approach), but explicit volumetric context processing satisfies the 3D/volumetric criterion.
title: Pancreas Segmentation with Probabilistic Map Guided Bi-directional Recurrent UNet
architecture: PBR-UNet: probabilistic-map-guided bi-directional recurrent 2.5D UNet (two-stage: M-FCN initial estimation + 2.5D UNet primary segmentation)
architecture_details: Stage 1: multi-view FCN (M-FCN) with three FCNs (coronal/sagittal/axial) fused by arithmetic averaging to produce pixel-level probabilistic maps. Stage 2: probabilistic maps of adjacent slices (guidance depth 2, 5 channels) combined with center slice into hybrid multi-channel data fed to 2.5D UNet (encoder blocks with residual convolutions, decoder with ordinary convolutions, 4 blocks each, skip connections); outputs iteratively update probabilistic maps in forward and backward recurrent passes (update weights lambda_new=lambda_ori=0.5); termination when DSC of consecutive predictions > 0.95 or max 5 iterations; multi-view fusion also applied at final stage
loss_function: Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) loss
preprocessing: CT HU truncation to [-100, 240] HU and normalization to zero mean/unit variance; ROI cropping of image and probabilistic maps based on binarized initial probabilistic maps (threshold 0.5) with padding margin of 20
postprocessing: Binarization of final probabilistic maps and de-cropping to original volume; bi-directional recurrent iterations until prediction stability (DSC > 0.95 between consecutive predictions, max 5 iterations)

screening_notes: Deep learning (CNN) is the primary method and CT is the modality, and the heart is the target structure, but processing is 2D slice-based only; 3D model creation is post-hoc polygon reconstruction, not 3D segmentation. screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: (1) DL primary — nnU-Net, 3D TransUNet, UNETR; (2) 3D volumetric — 3D nnU-Net config, 3D-adapted TransUNet, 3D UNETR on full CT volumes; (3) organ segmentation — LV, LA, LAA, AA, PV (cardiac chambers = anatomical structures); (4) CT angiography; (5) quantitative metrics — Dice, ICC, Bland-Altman; (6) novel contribution — first study to estimate SV/EF of LA, LV, and LAA simultaneously from CT via fully automatic 3D DL, plus novel 3D TransUNet adaptation (code released). screening_notes: Meets all six inclusion criteria: (1) DL primary method (slice classification CNN + 3D encoder–decoder); (2) true 3D/volumetric segmentation (3D dilated convolutions, 16×256×256 volumes, z-axis context explicitly leveraged); (3) 12 OARs segmented (brainstem, eyes, optic nerves, temporal lobes, parotids, TMJs, mandible); (4) CT modality; (5) Dice + 95% Hausdorff reported; (6) novel two-step contribution (slice classification to prune irrelevant slices, refined dilated-convolution 3D encoder–decoder). Not a survey, not tumor-only, not 2D-only. Routing: novel segmentation method → 'method' (not framework/review/benchmark).
title: A slice classification model-facilitated 3D encoder–decoder network for segmenting organs at risk in head and neck cancer
architecture: Two-step model: slice classification CNN + refined 3D encoder–decoder segmentation network
architecture_details: Slice classifier: depth-wise separable convolutions + max-pooling + global average pooling, 6 craniocaudal categories (95.99% accuracy). Segmentation: 3D encoder–decoder with 7 down-sampling and 7 up-sampling dilated convolution stacks (dilation rates 1, 2, 3, 4), SELU activations, extra skip concatenations between dilated stacks, input 16×256×256 with 3-slice overlay. One OAR-specific segmentation model per organ.
loss_function: Dice loss (segmentation); categorical cross-entropy (slice classification); Adam optimizer, lr 0.001
preprocessing: Axial resolution resampled to 1×1 mm (bilinear interpolation); augmentation: random rotation within 20°, random axial translation within 20 pixels
postprocessing: Probability maps binarized at 0.5; morphological erosion+dilation (circular kernel r=2 px, 1 iteration) to smooth edges; edge detection for contours; anatomical-consistency correction of slice-category predictions; 5 extra slices appended at category boundaries for OAR coverage
datasets: ["In-house H&N CT dataset (Peking University Third Hospital, 170 patients)"]

organs_segmented: ["brainstem", "right eye", "left eye", "right optic nerve", "left optic nerve", "right temporal lobe", "left temporal lobe", "right parotid", "left parotid", "right temporomandibular joint", "left temporomandibular joint", "mandible"]
comparison_methods: ["Segmentation-only ablation (same 3D encoder–decoder without slice classification)", "Literature context: Ibragimov & Xing CNN", "Tong et al. shape-representation FCNN", "Liang et al. detection+segmentation model", "AnatomyNet (Zhu et al.)"]
training_time: Not reported (early stopping on validation set)

future_work: Multi-label segmentation model (e.g., eyes and optic nerves jointly) to avoid edge overlap; add attention-based, boosting-based, and lifelong learning strategies

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: nnU-Net (3D U-Net variant) as primary method on 3D CT volumes; liver segmentation on LiTS/IRCAD; quantitative metrics reported (Dice 0.974, HD95 2.458mm, volume % error 1.92%). Borderline on novelty (criterion 7): it is an application of the off-the-shelf nnU-Net package v1.6.6 without architectural modification, but the paper adds a validated volume-estimation pipeline with 3D renderings and reports improved Dice over prior methods on the same train/test setup (H-DenseUNet 0.965, RA-UNet 0.961), which qualifies as a significant improvement/application contribution for this review. Not a framework paper: nnU-Net is used, not presented as the authors' contribution.
title: nnU-Net Deep Learning Method for Segmenting Parenchyma and Determining Liver Volume From Computed Tomography Images
architecture_details: nnunet Python package v1.6.6; self-configured 3D U-Net with 3x3x3 convolutions (batch norm + ReLU), 2x2x2 max pooling, up-convolutions with skip concatenation; ~19,069,955 trainable parameters

future_work: Incorporate hepatic vasculature and lobar anatomy; collect/annotate prospective data for generalizability across clinical situations and demographics; build nnU-Net models for other solid organs (kidneys, heart, lungs); extend to MRI

screening_notes: Hybrid pipeline using deep learning (2D U-Net + 3D FCN with 3D convolutions) as the core segmentation engine for CT liver segmentation (96.3% Dice), with a DRLSE level-set + FCM refinement stage for tumor. Segments liver (an organ), not tumor-only; 3D FCN provides volumetric context; quantitative metrics (DSC, VOE, RVD, ASD, RMSD) reported on ISICDM and LiTS; novel contribution via FCM-enhanced edge indicator and automatic DL-based level-set initialization. Minor caveat: tumor refinement is slice-wise 2D level-set, but overall pipeline is volumetric and DL-driven.
title: Deep Learning Initialized and Gradient Enhanced Level-set Based Segmentation for Liver Tumor from CT Images
architecture: Coarse-to-fine cascade: 2D U-Net -> 3D FCN -> DRLSE level-set with FCM-enhanced edge indicator
architecture_details: 2D slice-based U-Net (9 conv blocks, encoder-decoder with skip connections, Conv-BN-ReLU) for coarse liver localization; 3D patch-based fully convolutional network (7 conv blocks, 48x48x48 patches, 3 pooling/3 upsampling) for fine liver segmentation and coarse tumor localization; tumor refined via distance regularized level-set evolution (DRLSE) initialized from 3D FCN output, with edge indicator enhanced by unsupervised fuzzy c-means (FCM) probability maps (Canny edges on FCM membership); intensity truncation [0,200] HU preprocessing
loss_function: Not explicitly reported (binary segmentation with sigmoid output)
preprocessing: CT intensity truncation to fixed range [0,200] HU (mean±3std rule); resampling to 1x1x1 mm³; 2D slices resized to 256x256 for U-Net; liver-mask-based cropping for 3D FCN; tumor-based piecewise linear intensity normalization (99th percentile truncation) before level-set
postprocessing: Erosion + median filter of coarse tumor mask for level-set initialization; slice-wise DRLSE evolution with FCM-enhanced edge indicator; convexity analysis to detect failed 3D liver segmentation with fallback to 2D U-Net result

dataset_size: ISICDM: 24 training + 36 testing CT volumes; LiTS: 131 training + 70 testing CT volumes

inference_time: ~90 s per CT volume (367x367x45): 10 s for 2D U-Net coarse liver, 50 s for 3D FCN, 30 s for FCM + level-set; coarse-to-fine strategy reduces 400 s (whole-volume 3D FCN) to 60 s for DL stages

screening_notes: Novel CNN (PANet with prior attention + justified inception blocks) as primary method; processes full-size 3D CT volumes with 3x3x3 convolutions; segments 22 OARs (not tumors-only); quantitative evaluation with DSC, HD95, VCR and significance tests. Novel contribution: SRSF stepwise coarse-to-fine pipeline and PAI attention block. Not a review, not framework/tooling paper.
title: Prior Attention Enhanced Convolutional Neural Network Based Automatic Segmentation of Organs at Risk for Head and Neck Cancer Radiotherapy
architecture: PANet (Prior Attention enhanced CNN) within a Stepwise Refinement Segmentation Framework (SRSF)
architecture_details: U-Net-based pyramidal network with justified inception blocks (pooling path removed) and Prior Attention + learnable convolutional spatial attention (PAI block); three sequential stages: OAR-group segmentation (OGS via IPNet on half-resolution CT), large/easy OAR segmentation (LOS), small/difficult OAR segmentation (SOS); prior probability maps from earlier stages feed attention
loss_function: Combined Dice loss + Surface Distance (SD) loss: Loss = LossDice + alpha*LossSD (alpha=1, gamma=1)
preprocessing: CT intensity clipped to [WL-WW/2, WL+WW/2] and normalized to [-1,1]; half-resolution downsampling for OGS stage; augmentation via translation, rotation, noise addition
postprocessing: None reported (stepwise ROI localization is part of the pipeline, not post-hoc processing)

screening_notes: Novel CNN architecture (MPNet) as primary method; processes volumetric data via inter-slice 1x1x3 kernels plus tri-planar (axial/coronal/sagittal) integration — not independent 2D slices; liver segmentation on LiTS 2017 CT; reports Dice/VOE/ASD/MSD. All inclusion criteria met.
title: Automatic Liver Segmentation Using Multi-plane Integrated Fully Convolutional Neural Networks
venue: IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM)
architecture: MPNet: multi-plane integrated fully convolutional network
architecture_details: Symmetric encoder-decoder with 10 residual blocks; pseudo-3D factorized kernels (3x3x1 intra-slice + 1x1x3 inter-slice); dilated convolutions (rates 1-3); 2 downsampling layers; encoder-decoder feature concatenation; multi-scale prediction fusion; trained independently in axial, coronal, sagittal planes and averaged softmax at test time
loss_function: Dice loss
preprocessing: Resampled all scans to isotropic 1mm^3 resolution
postprocessing: None (authors emphasize no pre/post-processing beyond resampling)
dataset_size: 131 contrast-enhanced 3D abdominal CT scans (103 training, 28 testing)
comparison_methods: ["LiTS 2017 leaderboard top teams (ed10b047, hans.meine, medical, IeHealth, deepX, predible, chunliang, yaya)", "Christ et al. cascaded FCN+CRF", "Yang et al. DI2IN adversarial", "Dou et al. 3D DSN", "internal ablation: axial-only single plane"]
training_time: ~32.5h per plane; ~97h total for 3 planes (20k iterations, batch size 1, Adam lr=1e-3)
inference_time: 13-85s per subject single plane; 30-250s with multi-plane integration (depends on slice count)
limitations: Axial-only predictions failed on test volumes with few slices (cases 1, 2, 23); simple averaging of three planes may be suboptimal given differing resolution across views; dilated convolution showed no significant improvement though retained
future_work: Extend method to liver tumor segmentation

screening_notes: Novel architecture (CC-DenseUNet: DenseNet-121 encoder + U-Net + criss-cross attention bottleneck), primary method is deep learning. Uses CT volumes (LiTS, 3DIRCADb) and reports DSC, VOE, RAVD, ASD, RMSD. Segments liver (organ) plus liver tumors, so not tumor-only. Caveat: the model is 2.5D (three adjacent slices as input, predictions stacked into a 3D volume), not true 3D convolutions — is_3d=false — but it uses inter-slice volumetric context and volumetric output, so it does not meet the '2D slices independently without 3D context' exclusion.
title: CC-DenseUNet: Densely Connected U-Net with Criss-Cross Attention for Liver and Tumor Segmentation in CT Volumes
venue: IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM)
architecture: CC-DenseUNet: densely connected U-Net (DenseNet-121 backbone) with criss-cross attention (CCA) module at the bottleneck
architecture_details: 2.5D fully convolutional network: three adjacent slices fed as input, 3D segmentation volume assembled by stacking center-slice predictions; DenseNet-121 dense blocks in downsampling path; CCA (from CCNet) for non-local contextual aggregation; transfer learning from pre-trained DenseNet-121
loss_function: Weighted cross-entropy
preprocessing: HU windowing: LiTS [-200, 200] HU; 3DIRCADb truncated to [-100, 400] HU. Data augmentation: random elastic deformation, rotation, scaling (0.8-1.2)
postprocessing: None beyond stacking 2.5D center-slice predictions into a 3D volume; original slice size used at test time
dataset_size: LiTS: 131 training scans (100 train / 31 custom test; official 70-scan test set GT not public); 3DIRCADb: 20 venous-phase CT volumes, 15 with tumors used in 2-fold cross validation
comparison_methods: ["2D U-Net", "3D U-Net", "Cascaded U-Net (Christ et al.)", "DCNN (Han)", "H-DenseUNet"]
limitations: Not explicitly stated; implicit limitations include custom LiTS test split (official test ground truths unavailable), small 3DIRCADb cohort, and 2.5D rather than fully 3D processing
future_work: Not explicitly stated; conclusion notes potential for aiding clinicians with liver and tumor segmentation

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: CT volumes (3D), liver segmentation, quantitative evaluation (DSC, VOE, ASSD, MaxD), novel contribution (hybrid fusion of traditional region-based pipeline with 3D U-Net + GrowCut). Caveat lowering confidence: deep learning is a core component but not purely primary — the traditional method alone achieves DSC 0.94 on SLIVER and the paper's framing is a fusion. Retained because 3D U-Net is integral to the proposed method and the contribution (CNN+classical fusion) is a recognized DL-hybrid category. Single-organ (liver only), CT-only.
title: Automatic liver segmentation on CT images combining region-based techniques and convolutional features
venue: IEEE International Conference on Content-Based Multimedia Indexing (CBMI)
architecture: 3D U-Net fused with traditional region-based pipeline (region growing + Chan-Vese active contour + PDF thresholding + GrowCut)
architecture_details: Hybrid fusion: (1) traditional mask from abdominal-region extraction, PDF-based thresholding, active contour, iterative 2D region growing propagated on 3 axes combined by voxelwise OR; (2) 3D U-Net (Cicek et al.) prediction mask refined with anatomical constraints (abdomen restriction, largest connected component) and GrowCut; final mask = 0.5*M + 0.5*PM, followed by lung-based liver-heart separation
loss_function: Not reported
preprocessing: Abdominal region extraction via MIP + thresholding; HU-based rescaling to 16-bit; median filtering; spine-based automatic orientation correction (180-degree rotation if needed); removal of lower-right quarter; probability-density-function (normal kernel) based thresholding with peak analysis for high/low contrast; cavity filling; morphological opening
postprocessing: Cavity filling; morphological opening with spherical structuring element; largest connected component selection; GrowCut refinement (eroded foreground label, radius 5); weighted fusion with delta=0.5; automatic lung-based liver-heart separation via binary thresholding [-1024,-300] HU and connected-component filtering
dataset_size: SLIVER train: 20 CT scans; mixed dataset: 60 CT volumes (VISCERAL + SLIVER, 54 train / 6 test); private database: 8 abdominal CT scans
comparison_methods: ["van Rikxoort et al. (2007) voxel classification + atlas matching", "Zhang et al. (2010) statistical shape model", "Wu et al. (2016) supervoxel-based graph cuts", "Dou et al. (2016) 3D deeply supervised network", "Esfandiarkhani et al. (2017) generalized active shape model", "Ajani et al. (2018) sparse ensemble with ML contexts", "Ahmad et al. (2019) deep belief network"]
limitations: Undersegmentation at liver tip and at vessels near the boundary; undersegments when tumor is close to the liver boundary; large max surface distances (MaxD up to ~43-50 mm); 3D U-Net alone degrades sharply on unseen heterogeneous data (DSC 0.79-0.81) and 3 leave-one-out cases produced unusable masks due to limited training data; fusion evaluated on small private set (8 scans)
future_work: More sophisticated fusion of traditional and convolutional features; integrate top-down anatomical information into the network model to further enhance segmentation performance

screening_notes: Deep learning (cascaded fully convolutional networks, Caffe) is the primary segmentation method; segments liver (organ) plus liver tumor on CT volumes (3D-IRCADb-01); reports quantitative Dice (94.58% liver, 45.87% tumor); novel contribution is a normalization/3D augmentation pipeline (slice interpolation, organ-centered 3D geometric transformations). Borderline on the 3D criterion: the network itself is 2D slice-based, but 3D volumetric context is explicitly exploited in the data pipeline (volume construction, 3D rotations, oblique slice sampling), so exclusion criterion 3 does not apply. Tumor is not the only target — liver organ is segmented, so exclusion criterion 5 does not apply.
title: Medical Images Sequence Normalization and Augmentation: Improve Liver Tumor Segmentation From Small Dataset
venue: International Conference on Control, Robotics and Cybernetics (CRC)
architecture_details: Two-phase 2D FCN cascade based on Christ et al. (MICCAI 2016): stage 1 segments the liver and generates a liver ROI, stage 2 segments liver tumor within the ROI; dense CRF refinement used for liver segmentation; implemented in Caffe
loss_function: Not explicitly specified (SGD optimizer, learning rate 0.001, momentum 0.8, weight decay 0.0005)
preprocessing: Intensity normalization to [0, 2047]; removal of intensity levels with probability < 0.0005%; histogram shrinking and rescaling; thresholding to eliminate non-liver tissue intensities using labeled data (liver+tumor range approx. [700, 1400]); linear slice interpolation to fill gaps between slices
postprocessing: Dense conditional random field (CRF) applied to liver segmentation output
dataset_size: 20 CT volumes from 3D-IRCADb-01 (10 women, 10 men; 15 training / 5 validation, 2-fold cross validation); plus 1 real patient volume
comparison_methods: ["non-augmented dataset baseline", "un-normalized dataset", "normalized dataset (no augmentation)", "3D augmented dataset variants", "Christ et al. original CFCN results (reference only, different validation set)"]
training_time: Not reported (3D augmentation phase took several days)
limitations: Very small dataset (20 volumes); tumor Dice remains low (45.87%); results not directly comparable to the original CFCN paper due to different validation sets; intensity normalization uses a custom [0, 2047] scale rather than Hounsfield units
future_work: Expand the augmentation approach to other small datasets acquired from CT machines with different configurations

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: (1) DL is primary method — modified 3D V-Net with novel grouped attention module; (2) fully 3D volumetric processing of CT volumes; (3) segments anatomical cardiac structures (left atrium, pulmonary veins), not tumors; (4) Low-Dose CT modality; (5) reports DSC, ASD, HD with 5-fold cross-validation; (6) novel contribution — new grouped attention block (GAB) plus V-Net modifications (no residual connections, Instance Norm). Borderline note: PV/LA are cardiac substructures rather than parenchymal organs, but this is standard whole-heart/cardiac segmentation scope, not lesion-only (exclusion criterion 5 does not apply).
title: Automatic Pulmonary Vein and Left Atrium Segmentation for TAPVC Preoperative Evaluation Using V-Net with Grouped Attention
venue: IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society Conference (EMBC 2020)
architecture_details: V-Net with three modifications: (1) residual connections removed from encoder convolutions, (2) Batch Normalization replaced with Instance Normalization, (3) Grouped Attention Blocks (GAB) deployed in each decoder stage. GAB = K=4 independent Spatial-and-Channel Attention Blocks (SCABs, CBAM-inspired) combined with grouped convolution; spatial attention generated via convolutions instead of pooling.
loss_function: Generalized Dice Loss (GDL) with inverse-frequency class weights
preprocessing: Lung region extraction from whole 3D CT via OTSU thresholding (to save computation); Z-score normalization of CT volumes; data augmentation: random crop (patch size 208x96x208) and Gaussian noise
postprocessing: Connected component analysis: retain largest connected component per class (PV, LA) to remove small false positives
datasets: ["Private pediatric TAPVC dataset from Shanghai Children's Medical Center"]
dataset_size: 68 Low-Dose 3D CT scans (preoperative TAPVC pediatric patients); volumes 512x512x(112-640), typical spacing 0.35x0.35x0.625mm
comparison_methods: ["V-Net", "3D-UNet", "V-Net + SCAB (ablation)"]
training_time: Not mentioned (training: Adam, lr 0.001 halved on plateau, batch size 2, converges within 25 epochs x 200 iterations)
inference_time: ~400 milliseconds per 3D CT volume (vs. 2-3 hours manual segmentation)
limitations: Not explicitly stated in paper. Implicit: small single-center dataset (68 patients) of a rare congenital disease; relatively high HD variance (e.g., PV 12.627±6.724 mm) indicates inconsistent boundary accuracy; DSC values for PV are modest (~0.8).
future_work: Refine the model for better performance and expand the application to other cardiac structures.

screening_notes: Paper proposes a novel SAP (Segment and Pickup) framework with a new LS-ResNet architecture (3D U-Net-style encoder-decoder with long/short residual shortcuts) for pancreas segmentation from abdominal CT. Deep learning is the primary method (region growing/connected-domain is only a pickup refinement step). Processes 3D volumes with 64x64x64 patches and 3D convolutions (3x3x3). Segments the pancreas (an organ) on the NIH Pancreas CT dataset (82 scans). Reports quantitative metrics: DSC 86.96%, Jaccard 74.62%, Precision 88.21% with 4-fold cross-validation. Novel methodological contribution (new framework + architecture) vs. C2F/LAS baselines. All inclusion criteria met; no exclusion criteria triggered. Note: 'framework' in the paper title refers to a methodological pipeline, not open-source tooling, so it is NOT routed as study_type 'framework'.
title: 3D Segment and Pickup Framework for Pancreas Segmentation
authors: Kaiyi Peng et al. (with Bin Fang)
venue: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
architecture: LS-ResNet (long and short residual network): 3D U-Net-style encoder-decoder, used within the proposed Segment and Pickup (SAP) framework with two networks (SeedNet and SegNet)
architecture_details: Encoder: 3x3x3 conv + batch norm + ReLU blocks with max pooling (2x2x2, stride 2); short-range residual shortcuts added after the first and second pooling layers. Decoder: 4x4x4 deconvolutions (stride 2) with a long-range shortcut summing encoder output with deconvolution output. SeedNet produces a rough clean seed segmentation from the whole CT; SegNet segments pancreas within a contour ROI (voxels within Euclidean distance d=16 of pancreas); final result picked via connected-domain/region-growing using SeedNet as seed.
loss_function: Standard cross-entropy loss (negative log-likelihood); SegNet loss computed only within the contour ROI (ROId = {x | D(x) < d})
preprocessing: HU clipping to [-100, 240] and rescaling to [0, 1]; data augmentation: rotation (90/180/270 degrees) and flips along axial, sagittal, coronal axes; resolutions kept unchanged; patch-based sampling of 64x64x64 with step 8x8x8
postprocessing: Region growing / connected component analysis to pick up final pancreas segmentation from SegNet output noise using SeedNet result; at test time output patches cropped to 16x16x16 and combined with step size 8x8x8
dataset_size: 82 contrast-enhanced abdominal CT scans (4-fold cross-validation)
comparison_methods: ["Zhu et al. 3D ResNet coarse-to-fine (84.06%)", "Man et al. 2D MV UNet with deep Q learning (85.43%)", "Chen et al. 3D UNet (84.57%)", "Li et al. 2D UNet multiscale receptive field (79.70%)", "Baseline 3D ResNet with C2F (86.25%)", "State-of-the-art: Zhu et al. (84.59%), Xue et al. (85.9%), Man et al. (85.93%), Khosravan et al. PAN (84.57%), Chen et al. (85.22%), Li et al. (87.57%)"]
limitations: Framework-level improvement alone is insufficient: authors note some complex network architectures bring large performance gains and their method is outperformed by Li et al. (87.57% DSC), indicating 'our improvement to the framework is only one aspect of the improvement of the complete pancreas segmentation method'. SegNet alone produces large noise regions requiring SeedNet pickup. Training-time ROI relies on ground-truth annotation contour distance.
future_work: Improve the network architecture ('we will pay more attention to improvement of network architecture'), combining appropriate framework with excellent network structure for best performance.
components: N/A (method paper, not an open-source framework/tooling paper)

title: A Simple and Robust Framework for Cross-Modality Medical Image Segmentation applied to Vision Transformers
venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision Workshops (ICCVW 2023)
architecture: Conditional Vision Transformer (C-ViT) encoder with U-Net style decoder (applied to Swin-UNETR); conditional 3D residual U-Net
architecture_details: Replaces Layer Normalization in transformer blocks with Conditional Instance Normalization (CIN) whose parameters are switched based on input modality; framework also applied to 3D UNet with pre-activation residual blocks (Valindria et al. baseline); trained with non-registered interleaved mixed MRI+CT data in a single conditional model; sliding-window inference with 0.5 overlap
loss_function: Dice Loss + Focal Loss (L = λD·L_Dice + λF·L_Focal with λD = λF = 1)
preprocessing: N4 bias field correction for MRI; resampling to isotropic spacing; intensity normalization to [0,1]; random 96x96x96 crops per volume (transformer sub-patches 16x16x16); data augmentation via random intensity shifting/scaling and random flips in all three dimensions
postprocessing: None explicitly reported (sliding-window inference with 0.5 overlap used at validation/test)
dataset_size: 40 volumes total (20 MRI + 20 CT); two-fold cross-validation with 10 CT + 20 MRI per fold for training
organs_segmented: ["whole heart (WH)", "left ventricle blood cavity (LV)", "right ventricle blood cavity (RV)", "left atrium blood cavity (LA)", "right atrium blood cavity (RA)", "left ventricle myocardium (MYO)", "ascending aorta (AA)", "pulmonary artery (PA)"]
other_metrics: {"cross_validation_mean_dice": "C-ViT 91.18% ± 0.68 vs conditional UNet 90.76% ± 0.55 (two-fold CV on MM-WHS CT)", "note": "Dice is the only quantitative metric reported; C-ViT PA value missing from extracted text (approx. 86.4 computable from reported average of 89.33)"}
comparison_methods: ["Single-modality UNet baseline (Valindria et al.)", "Fine-tuning", "Joint training", "X-shaped dual-stream architecture (Valindria et al., WACV 2018)", "Cycle- and shape-consistent GAN translation (Zhang et al., 2019)", "Online mutual knowledge distillation (Li et al., 2020)", "Swin-UNETR baseline"]
gpu_used: Multiple NVIDIA V100 GPUs (IDRIS HPC/AI cluster)
